enforced_by: the video teardown's doctrine read and the AI brief's frames; recorded as unknown, never refused
note: One list per visual dimension — shot, angle, camera, composition, light, colour, capture (the owner, 2026-10-13); the asset is the dimension.

rows.name: off-centre
rows.what: The subject on a third, room on the other side.

extra.real: Never perfectly on the third — a little loose, as a person frames it.

rows.name: centred
rows.what: The subject dead centre, square to camera.

extra.real: Only for direct address to the lens; the selfie is naturally centred.

rows.name: foreground-frame
rows.what: Something in the foreground frames the subject — a doorway, a shelf, a shoulder.

extra.real: The foreground soft and slightly out of focus.

rows.name: negative-space
rows.what: Empty space around a small subject.

extra.real: A real empty wall or sky, never a backdrop.

rows.name: lived-in
rows.what: A full, real frame — the place's clutter around the subject.

extra.real: The objects the avatar actually owns, a little untidy.
